key_insight: When diagnoses include cases not detectable from model inputs, selective testing can make AI predictions appear useful in tested patients yet reverse in untested patients.
clinical_relevance: ECG-based ACS models may not generalize beyond catheterized patients, highlighting the importance of input-detectable targets and evaluation in the intended population.
method: Formalized and simulated selective-label bias when targets include input-undetectable cases.
Fine-tuned three ECG foundation models on revascularization as an ACS proxy.
Compared performance across catheterized and untested patients and ECG-visible versus unstable-angina targets.
evidence_signal: Revascularization-trained models achieved AUROC 0.740–0.770 in catheterized patients but 0.381–0.478 for 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events in untested patients; ECG-visible-target models retained discrimination at 0.680–0.709.
watch_item: Revascularization and 30-day adverse events are different proxy outcomes, complicating interpretation of performance across tested and untested populations.
paper_title: Target Recoverability under Selective Labels: A Failure Mode in ECG-Based Acute Coronary Syndrome Prediction
